issues.legal_issue: The additional-accommodation eviction provision applies only when the landlord and tenant occupy different portions of the same building, not separate buildings owned by the landlord.
material_facts: The landlord occupied one building for his residence and business and sought additional business space.
The tenant occupied an adjoining building that the landlord had acquired separately and that had previously been owned by another person.

The buildings were separated by a single wall and were under common ownership, but the tenant’s building could be sold and transferred without affecting the landlord’s possession and enjoyment of his building.
issues.conclusion: The landlord could not obtain eviction under the additional-accommodation provision because the tenant occupied a separate building, not another portion of the building occupied by the landlord. The appeal was allowed and the dismissal of the eviction petition was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(3)(c) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960 permits a landlord occupying only part of a building to seek possession of another portion of that same building for additional residential or business accommodation. It requires oneness of the building, not merely common ownership. Section 2(iii), defining “building,” does not permit separate adjoining buildings in different occupation to be treated as one integrated building for this purpose. Whether adjoining premises are parts of one building may be assessed by whether one can be sold and its purchaser placed in possession without affecting the landlord’s possession and enjoyment of the other; a common wall does not determine the issue. The Court referred to Balaganesan Metals v. M.N. Shanmugham Chetty, JT 1987 (2) SC 247, M. Ramaswamy Naidu v. P. Venkateswarlu, Vol. II (1961) 1 A.W.R. 400, and Balaiah v. Lachaiah, AIR 1965 AP 435.

predicates.additional_accommodation_eviction_case: A landlord seeks a tenant’s eviction to obtain additional residential or business accommodation.
predicates.landlord_and_tenant_occupy_different_bui: The landlord occupies one building while the tenant occupies a separate building, rather than another portion of the landlord’s building.
predicates.tenant_building_independently_transferab: The tenant’s building can be sold and its purchaser placed in possession without affecting the landlord’s possession and enjoyment of the other building.
predicates.additional_accommodation_eviction_not_au: The landlord cannot obtain eviction on the ground of needing additional accommodation.

issues.definition: When an additional-accommodation eviction case concerns a tenant in a different building that can be transferred independently without affecting the landlord’s building, the output is that eviction on that ground is not authorized.
